decisions.reason: As a complementary sensing module with still-plausible demand and relatively low carrying cost on the shared platform, it is worth keeping even though its overlap with other environmental sensors makes its upside somewhat uncertain.
Because it is a third-generation replacement of a core measurement function, its value is largely proven and it supports the platform broadly, so dropping it would destroy more value than it saves.
The CAN bus interface fits the firm's automation and embedded customer base well, and maintaining it preserves a useful option at modest ongoing cost despite being more niche than core I/O modules.

A dedicated CO2 module has clear application value for schools, companies, and prototyping users, so the firm is likely to retain this low-cost option unless component or support burdens rise materially.
